leftEvidence.title: A man is delivered to Satan with flesh, spirit, and the Lord’s day in view

points.label: Stated purpose
points.left: A man is delivered to Satan with flesh, spirit, and the Lord’s day in view
points.right: Hymenaeus and Alexander are handed to Satan. The stated aim is that they learn not to blaspheme.

points.label: Community setting
points.left: The scene includes reported sexual immorality, pride, and mourning. It also includes communal judgment, gathered authority, and delivery to Satan. It also includes flesh, spirit, and the Lord’s day. Together, these details are linked in the passage.
points.right: The scene includes prophecies, warfare, and faith. It also includes conscience, shipwreck, and named people. It also includes delivery to Satan and instruction not to blaspheme. Together, these details close the charge.

payload.posture: Read both WEBU passages side by side. Keep each passage’s actors, setting, order, and identity claims distinct.

rightEvidence.title: Hymenaeus and Alexander are handed to Satan. The stated aim is that they learn not to blaspheme.

payload.tension: Both use the phrase “delivered to Satan,” but they state different purposes in different communities.
payload.title: Two people delivered to Satan
